result.question: Give me a sample-by-sample picture of the fault gases in Transformer 1 at MAIN between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. For each sample, list hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Name the dominant gas, meaning the one with the highest ppm, and give its percentage of the five-gas total. Then tell me whether the dominant gas changed at any point in the window. Say what that shift points to, for example hydrogen pointing to partial discharge, ethylene to a hotter thermal fault, or acetylene to arcing. Also rank the five gases by their percentage growth from the first to the last sample. If a gas is null in a sample, leave it out of that sample's total and mark it as missing. If fewer than two samples have all five gases, give the ranking from the latest reading alone and say that no trend could be established.
result.answer:
Nothing further is needed — all four samples in the window were returned with all five gases populated, so I can compute everything directly.

**Transformer 1 (MAIN), 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19 — sample-by-sample fault gases (ppm)**

| Timestamp | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 | 5-gas total | Dominant gas | Share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15T00:00 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32409 | Ethylene | 51.48% |
| 2024-01-16T00:00 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 32056 | Ethylene | 51.47% |
| 2024-01-17T00:00 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 32308 | Ethylene | 51.69% |
| 2024-01-18T00:00 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 32307 | Ethylene | 51.38% |

No gas was null in any sample, so nothing was excluded or marked missing.

**Did the dominant gas change?** No. Ethylene was the dominant gas in all four samples, holding a steady ~51.4–51.7% of the five-gas total. Because there was no shift, there is no change in fault signature to interpret. The persistent ethylene dominance (with methane and ethane as the next largest and acetylene near-zero) points consistently to a high-temperature thermal fault (T2/T3, >300–700 °C range) — not partial discharge (which would show hydrogen dominant) and not arcing (which would show a rising acetylene share). Note that the absolute levels are very high, so the condition itself warrants attention even though it is stable over this window.

**Ranking by percentage growth, first sample (01-15) → last sample (01-18):**

1. Hydrogen: 2845 → 2900, **+1.93%**
2. Acetylene: 7 → 7, **0.00%**
3. Ethane: 5467 → 5450, **−0.31%**
4. Ethylene: 16684 → 16600, **−0.50%**
5. Methane: 7406 → 7350, **−0.76%**

All movements are within ±2% — essentially flat, with a slight hydrogen uptick and marginal declines in the hydrocarbon gases. Four complete samples were available, so a trend could be established (stable, no escalation over the window).
